Seminar Title:

Noninvasive and Minimally invasive bio sensing platforms for early detection and staging of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD)

Seminar Type:

Abstract:

Diseases related to metabolic dysfunction pose a major issue in terms of global health. Existing diagnostic techniques are based on invasive biopsy procedures, whilst biomarkers employed in diagnostics do not have enough sensitivity to enable the identification of preclinical stages of the disease. &nbspThis study aims at the creation of new bio-sensing platforms with the help of molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) being used as artificial antibodies for the non-invasive detection of metabolic dysfunction-associated biomarkers. The research will apply a step-by-step method involving computer-aided design, polymer synthesis, sensor engineering, and clinical validation to achieve the objectives of the study. First, density functional theory (DFT) will be used to design MIPs featuring specific protein epitopes in an efficient way and to predict the interactions between the monomers and the templates at an atomic scale before they are synthesized. Second, the created MIPs will be synthesized on the basis of the polymerization technology in order to make the recognition sites that exhibit a high affinity. Third, the synthesized MIPs will be incorporated into the electrochemical sensing systems for biomarker detection. Fourth, the efficiency of the sensors will be tested according to state-of-the-art diagnostic techniques. The expected outcomes include developing affordable yet reliable biosensors capable of prompt diagnosis and accurate staging of diseases related to metabolic disturbance. The application of DFT-guided MIP design is a significant development that allows a considerable progress in biosensor design as it facilitates the transition from empirical biosensor development to rational one. &nbspThe proposed research addresses an important problem related to the development of diagnostic practices that would ensure a non-invasive approach to the diagnosis which makes it possible to monitor the patients periodically, intervene earlier, and ensure personalized management of the disease. The successful implementation of these technologies could reduce invasive procedures, improve patient adherence, and facilitate more effective therapeutic intervention.&nbsp
